report.tagline: One workspace for notes, docs, wikis, project trackers and AI agents, built from blocks you can rearrange.
report.simpleSummary: Notion is like a box of Lego for your work. Every page is made of blocks: text, to-do lists, tables, images. You can turn a simple page into a team wiki, a task board or a reading list without writing code. It is free for one person, and teams pay per member each month, with AI that can write, search and now do tasks for you.

keyNumbers.note: Sacra estimate, August 2026. Notion said it passed $500M in September 2025 and $600M by December 2025. Not audited.

keyNumbers.label: Revenue growth
keyNumbers.note: Sacra estimate, mid-2026. Fast for a 13-year-old company, driven mostly by AI.

keyNumbers.label: Users
keyNumbers.note: Company figure reported in 2026. Counts sign-ups, not daily active users, so real active use is lower.

keyNumbers.label: Share of revenue from AI
keyNumbers.note: Reported in December 2025 news on the share sale. Hard to verify, since AI is now bundled into the Business plan.

keyNumbers.label: Valuation
keyNumbers.note: Employee share sale of about $270M to $300M, January 2026. Notion is reported to be cash-flow positive.

keyNumbers.label: Big company reach
keyNumbers.note: Company claim, 2026. Means some team at the company uses it, not that the whole company runs on it.

overview.whatItDoes: Notion lets people and teams write, plan and store knowledge in one place. Pages can hold text, tables, boards, calendars and links to other pages. Notion AI can write drafts, answer questions from your pages and connected apps, and since 2025 can run agents that do multi-step work on their own.
howItWorks: Everything is a block. You type '/' to add a heading, a checklist, a table, an image or an embed, and drag blocks around.
Databases are tables where each row is a full page. The same data can be shown as a table, a Kanban board, a calendar or a timeline.
Templates let you start fast. Notion and its community share thousands of ready-made setups, from habit trackers to company wikis.
Teams share a workspace with permissions, comments and live editing.
Notion AI and Notion Agent answer questions, write, fill databases and, with Custom Agents (2026), run in the background on schedules or triggers.
Connectors pull in Slack, Google Drive, GitHub and more, so search and AI can see work that lives outside Notion.
overview.valueProposition: Instead of paying for five tools (docs, wiki, task tracker, notes, AI assistant) and copying work between them, a team gets one flexible tool that it can shape to how it already works.

personas.name: Student or self-organiser
personas.description: A college student or young professional who uses Notion for free to plan studies, track habits and save notes. Often found Notion through a YouTube template video.
goals: Keep notes, deadlines and goals in one place
Make a setup that looks good and feels personal
frustrations: Blank page is overwhelming at first
App feels slow on a cheap phone or weak network

personas.name: Startup operator
personas.description: Ops lead or founder at a 10 to 200 person company who sets up the company wiki, roadmap and hiring tracker in Notion.
goals: One source of truth for the whole company
Replace several paid tools with one
Get new hires up to speed fast
frustrations: Wiki gets messy and out of date
Search does not always find the right page
AI now needs the costlier Business plan

personas.name: Product or engineering team lead
personas.description: Runs sprints, specs and meeting notes. Compares Notion with Jira, Linear and Confluence.
goals: Write specs and track work in one place
Get meeting notes and action items without typing
frustrations: Weaker than Jira or Linear for heavy engineering workflows
Hard to control who sees what in big workspaces

personas.name: Enterprise IT buyer
personas.description: Approves tools at a large company. Cares about security, admin controls and cost per seat.
goals: Safe AI that does not leak company data
Single sign-on, audit logs and admin controls
Fewer overlapping tools to pay for
frustrations: Already pays for Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace
Teams build Notion setups in different ways, so it gets messy
Usage-based AI credits make costs harder to predict

painPoints.pain: Work is spread across many tools: docs in one place, tasks in another, notes somewhere else.
painPoints.howSolved: Docs, wikis, databases and tasks live in the same workspace and link to each other.

painPoints.pain: Rigid tools force a team into one way of working.
painPoints.howSolved: Blocks and databases let teams build their own system without code.

painPoints.pain: Starting from a blank page is hard.
painPoints.howSolved: Thousands of free and paid templates in the Notion Marketplace give a ready starting point.

painPoints.pain: People cannot find the answer that someone already wrote down.
painPoints.howSolved: Notion AI searches across pages and connected apps like Slack and Google Drive and answers in plain language with links.

painPoints.pain: Meeting notes and status updates eat up hours each week.
painPoints.howSolved: AI Meeting Notes records and summarises calls. Custom Agents can write weekly updates or triage requests on a schedule.

painPoints.pain: Paying for a separate AI tool on top of other software.
painPoints.howSolved: AI is bundled into the Business plan, so the team does not need a second subscription for search and writing help.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Every piece of content is a block that can be moved, nested or turned into another type.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: This is the core idea. It makes Notion flexible enough to replace many simple tools.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Tables where each row is a page, shown as table, board, calendar, timeline or gallery.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Turns notes into a working system like a CRM, content calendar or roadmap. This is what makes teams stay.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A store of free and paid templates made by Notion and by creators.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Brings new users in through creators and shortens time to first value. Creators earn money, so they keep promoting Notion.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Writes, summarises, answers questions across the workspace and connected apps, and since September 2025 can carry out multi-step tasks.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Main reason revenue grew about 82% in a year. Pushes teams from cheaper plans up to Business.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Agents a team sets up once that run in the background, for example to sort bug reports or write a Monday update. Over one million were built in two months of 2026.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Moves Notion from a place you write to a place where work gets done. Adds Notion's first pay-per-use revenue at $10 per 1,000 credits.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Records a call, writes a summary and action items straight into a Notion page.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Gives a daily reason to open Notion and puts it up against tools like Otter and Granola.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Share a page with a teammate, a guest or the public web, with live editing and comments.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Every shared page shows Notion to someone new, which is how one user turns into a whole team.

steps.detail: Watches a YouTube or Instagram video of a 'student dashboard' built in Notion.
Creates an account with Google in under a minute.
Clicks the creator's template link and copies it into their own workspace.
Adds their own subjects and deadlines, changes icons and covers.
Opens it each morning to check tasks. The more they add, the harder it is to leave.
Shares a study page with classmates, who sign up to edit it.
The ops lead already uses Notion personally and creates a team workspace.
Moves onboarding docs, policies and the org chart into a company home page.
Each invite adds a member. The free plan's limits push the team toward Plus.
Hiring tracker, roadmap and meeting notes move in, so people now open Notion daily.
Wants AI search across Slack and Drive, which needs the Business plan at $20 per member per month (yearly).
Finance agrees because it can cancel a separate wiki tool and an AI tool.
Every Friday someone spends an hour writing the sprint update from the task database.
Describes the job in plain words: read the sprint board, write a summary, post to Slack.
Picks which pages, databases and connected apps the agent can read and edit.
Runs it every Friday at 4 pm, or whenever a task changes status.
Checks the output and edits the instructions to fix mistakes.
Other teams copy the agent. Credit use grows, which adds usage revenue for Notion.

businessModel.summary: Notion makes money from monthly seats: a team pays for each member. Individuals use it free, which feeds the funnel. AI is now the main reason teams pay more, bundled into the Business plan, and from May 2026 agents add a pay-per-use charge on top, which is usage-based pricing.

revenueStreams.detail: Small teams pay about $10 per member per month (yearly) for unlimited blocks, file uploads and basic collaboration.
About $20 per member per month (yearly). Since May 2025 this plan includes Notion AI, search across connected apps and meeting notes. This is the main growth driver.
Custom priced deals with security, admin and audit features. Larger and stickier than self-serve teams.
Custom Agents use credits at $10 per 1,000, launched May 2026. Notion's first pay-per-use revenue line.

businessModel.pricing: Free for individuals. Plus about $10 per member per month billed yearly ($12 monthly). Business about $20 per member per month yearly ($24 monthly), includes Notion AI. Enterprise is custom. Custom Agent credits $10 per 1,000 (2026). The old $8 to $10 AI add-on is no longer sold to new Free or Plus users.
costDrivers: AI model costs paid to providers like Anthropic and OpenAI on every AI request
Cloud hosting and storage for billions of blocks
Engineering and design staff, about 1,000 employees
Sales and support teams for enterprise deals
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a 20-person startup on Business at $20 per member: about $400 a month, or $4,800 a year. Classic software costs very little per extra seat, so most of that used to be profit. AI changes this. If each member asks AI 10 to 20 questions a day, model costs could be a few dollars per member per month, so Notion might keep around 70% to 80% of the seat price instead of 90%. Heavy agent users who burn credits pay extra, which protects the margin. The free users cost money to host but are cheap marketing: some later bring their team, and one team can be worth thousands of dollars a year. These margin figures are rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Community-led growth: creators on YouTube, Instagram and TikTok sell or share templates, and every template brings new sign-ups
Shared pages: every public or shared page shows Notion to a new person
Bottom-up adoption: one person uses it, then invites the team, then the company pays
Student and startup programs give free or cheap plans so habits start early
Search and AI chat traffic for 'Notion template for X'
whatBringsUsersBack: Daily task lists and meeting notes live there
The more pages and links a team adds, the more painful it is to move out
AI answers get better as more company knowledge is stored
Custom Agents run on their own and post results, pulling people back to check
growth.moat: A team's moat is its own content. After two years in Notion a company has thousands of linked pages, databases and agents, and moving them is painful. On top of that sits a creator community of templates and tutorials that no rival has matched. The weakness is that Microsoft and Google already sit on most company data and can bundle similar AI for free.

competitors.name: Microsoft 365 (Loop, OneNote, Copilot)
competitors.positioning: Already paid for by most large companies, with Copilot AI on top.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Notion is one flexible tool rather than many apps, and is loved by startups and younger teams. Microsoft wins on bundling and IT trust.

competitors.name: Google Workspace (Docs, Gemini)
competitors.positioning: Simple docs and sheets that almost everyone knows, with Gemini AI built in.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Notion adds databases, wikis and agents in the same place. Google Docs is easier for one-off documents.

competitors.name: Atlassian Confluence and Jira
competitors.positioning: The standard wiki and task tracker for engineering teams in big companies.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Notion is easier to learn and nicer to write in. Confluence and Jira are deeper for strict engineering workflows.

competitors.name: ClickUp
competitors.positioning: All-in-one work tool, heavier on project management.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Notion is cleaner and more writing-first. ClickUp packs in more task features but feels busier.

competitors.name: Obsidian
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Notion is for teams and lives in the cloud. Obsidian wins with people who want files on their own device.

northStar.metric: Weekly active teams doing collaborative work (teams where 3 or more members edit or use AI on shared pages in a week)
northStar.why: Notion's money comes from teams, and teams stay only when many members rely on it every week. One person writing alone can be free forever. A team editing and asking AI together shows real value and predicts upgrades.

guardrailMetrics: Page load time on large workspaces and on mobile
Share of AI answers flagged as wrong or unhelpful
AI model cost per paid seat
Support tickets about surprise bills from agent credits
strengths: Very flexible: one tool can be a wiki, task board, CRM and notes app
Huge free creator community making templates and tutorials, which acts as free marketing
Strong brand with students and startups, who carry it into their next job
Fast AI revenue growth while staying cash-flow positive
Clean, calm design that people enjoy using
weaknesses: Gets slow with very large databases and on weaker phones and networks
Flexibility means messy workspaces; many teams struggle to keep wikis tidy
Limited offline use compared with Obsidian or OneNote
Side products have struggled: Notion Mail is being shut down in 2026 and Notion Calendar has had few updates
Moving AI into the Business plan raised prices for small teams that only wanted AI
risks: Microsoft and Google bundle AI into tools companies already pay for, making Notion feel like an extra cost
AI-native tools and general chat assistants like ChatGPT and Claude can write docs and answer questions without a workspace
AI model prices and supply depend on outside providers
Data privacy rules for AI in Europe and other markets
Stronger competition for teams after rivals were bought and funded, such as Airtable joining Bending Spoons in 2026
userComplaints: The app is slow to load big pages, especially on mobile
Search does not find the right page, even after AI search improvements
AI is now locked to the Business plan, so small teams feel forced to upgrade
Too flexible: hard to know how to set up and easy to make a mess
Usage-based agent credits make bills harder to predict

improvementIdeas.problem: Wikis go stale and messy, so people stop trusting them.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: AI flags out-of-date pages, duplicates and broken links each week and suggests fixes. Teams trust the wiki and use it more.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of pages viewed in last 90 days; AI answer accuracy rating

improvementIdeas.idea: Lite AI pack for Plus teams
improvementIdeas.problem: Small teams feel pushed to Business at double the price just for AI.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: A small monthly AI credit pack for Plus keeps price-sensitive teams and becomes a step toward Business.

improvementIdeas.idea: Agent cost preview and budget caps
improvementIdeas.problem: Admins fear surprise bills from usage-based agent credits.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Show estimated monthly credit cost before an agent goes live, with team-level caps. More teams will try agents.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of Business workspaces with at least one active agent; billing complaints

improvementIdeas.problem: The mobile app feels slow for quick notes, so people use other apps.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: A light, offline-first quick note screen that syncs later. More daily mobile opens.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Mobile daily active users; time from app open to first keystroke

improvementIdeas.problem: New teams do not know how to structure a workspace.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Ask three questions on sign-up (team type, size, tools used) and auto-build a starter workspace with sample data and an agent.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Week-one invites per workspace; 30-day team retention

pmLessons: Templates turned users into marketers. Notion let creators earn from templates, so thousands of people taught the product for free.
A flexible product needs strong starting points. Without templates and guidance, freedom feels like a blank page.
Adding AI to an existing product works best when it uses data the product already holds. Notion AI is useful because it can read your team's pages.
Bundling AI into a higher plan raised revenue fast, but it also annoyed small teams. Pricing changes always have winners and losers.
Focus matters. Notion's core grew while side apps like Mail were shut down.

interviewQuestions.question: Notion has about 100 million users but most pay nothing. How would you increase the share of free users who turn into paying teams?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split free users into solo, students and early teams. Focus on the moment one person invites others. Ideas: team trial on first invite, AI preview limits, team templates. Metric: free-to-paid team conversion within 60 days.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Notion AI stay inside the Business plan or become a separate add-on again?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue per seat, upgrade rate and churn under both. Think about small teams vs. larger companies, and AI model costs. Suggest a middle path like a credit pack, and say how you would test it.

interviewQuestions.question: Design Notion for a first-time user in a small Indian town on a low-end Android phone.
interviewQuestions.hint: Start with the user: weak network, small screen, maybe a local language. Ideas: offline-first, lighter pages, voice input in Hindi, ready student templates. Success metric: week-two retention for this group.

interviewQuestions.question: What should be the north star metric for Custom Agents?
interviewQuestions.hint: Avoid 'agents created'. Prefer value delivered, like weekly successful agent runs that a human accepted without edits. Add guardrails: error rate, cost per run, admin complaints.

interviewQuestions.question: Microsoft adds a free Notion-like tool to Microsoft 365. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Do not panic or cut prices first. Look at who is most at risk (big companies on Microsoft). Double down on what Microsoft lacks: community templates, agents across many tools, ease of use. Make importing and exporting easy.

glossary.meaning: Growth that comes from users and creators teaching and promoting the product to each other, not from paid ads.
When individual workers start using a tool first and the company pays for it later.
One paid user licence; teams pay a price per seat each month.
The money a company expects to earn in a year from subscriptions, based on current customers; often called ARR.
What investors think the whole company is worth, based on the price they pay for shares.
The company takes in more cash than it spends in a period.
Charging by how much you use something, like credits for agent runs, instead of a fixed monthly price.
The one number a team watches most because it best shows users getting real value.
How much revenue you keep from last year's customers this year, including upgrades and minus cancellations.
The share of customers who stop paying in a period.
The share of users or teams who keep using the product over time.
AI that can carry out several steps of a task on its own, not just answer one question.
A number that must not get worse while you try to improve the main metric.
Something that makes it hard for competitors to copy a product or win its customers.

assumptions: The $865M yearly revenue figure is a Sacra estimate, not a number Notion has published.
AI model cost per seat and the 70% to 80% margin range are our rough estimates.
Prices are US list prices from late 2025 and 2026; regional prices may differ.
The north star metric is our proposal; Notion has not published its own.
The '100 million users' figure counts accounts, so the active user base is likely much smaller.
